content.overview: BNS s. 213 — Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it. BNS restatement of IPC 179. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 179. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 213 is the rule on “Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it”. The section provides that whoever refuses to bind himself by an oath or affirmation to state the truth, when required so to bind himself by a public servant legally competent to require that he shall so bind himself, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 213 exists so that “Refusing oath or affirmation when duly required by public servant to make it” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Summons, proclamations, false information — and the recast suicide-attempt-to-coerce offence.
